name: AeroSandbox
summary: Python aircraft design and optimization environment using automatic differentiation and composable engineering analyses. Useful for rapid aerodynamic design exploration and multidisciplinary studies before committing to higher-fidelity CFD evaluations.
caveat: Many included methods are reduced-fidelity engineering models; do not equate all analyses with Navier–Stokes CFD.

name: Chaospy
summary: Numerical toolbox for polynomial chaos, sampling and quadrature. Useful for propagating uncertain flow parameters through CFD surrogates or moderately priced solvers and building nonintrusive uncertainty-expansion experiments.
caveat: High-dimensional or discontinuous response surfaces may require alternatives to a simple polynomial expansion.

name: Dakota
summary: Design exploration framework combining optimization, parameter estimation, sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification. Useful for managing repeated CFD evaluations and propagating uncertain inputs through external engineering simulation models.
caveat: Requires a working simulation interface and can demand many expensive flow evaluations.

name: foamlib
summary: Python interface for OpenFOAM files, cases and execution. Useful for reproducible parameter studies, programmatic field access and reducing repetitive case-management steps around an existing OpenFOAM installation.
caveat: OpenFOAM must be installed separately; confirm support for the selected distribution and file types.

name: MPhys
summary: Standardizes high-fidelity multiphysics problems within OpenMDAO using modular conventions and solver integrations. Useful for assembling CFD–structures or aerothermal studies while preserving coupling and derivative interfaces across disciplines.
caveat: It is an integration layer; individual examples require compatible external solvers and their dependencies.

name: OpenMDAO
summary: Python framework for tightly coupled systems analysis and multidisciplinary optimization. Useful for connecting CFD, structures and engineering models while managing derivatives, nonlinear coupling and parallel model execution.
caveat: CFD analysis components and reliable derivatives must be supplied; it does not replace a flow solver.

name: OpenTURNS
summary: C++ and Python library for probabilistic modelling and uncertainty treatment in industrial studies. Useful for wrapping CFD evaluations, defining uncertain inputs and constructing reliability, sensitivity or surrogate analyses.
caveat: Physics and solver interfaces remain application-specific; verify sampling accuracy and assumptions about input distributions.

name: pyOptSparse
summary: Framework for defining and solving constrained nonlinear optimization problems with sparse derivatives. Useful as an optimization driver around aerodynamic CFD models and other expensive engineering analyses with many constraints.
caveat: Some optimizer backends require separate proprietary licenses; check the chosen backend and installation.

name: RAVEN
summary: Simulation workflow framework for uncertainty quantification, optimization, model reduction and probabilistic risk analysis. Useful for orchestrating external CFD studies, sampling parameter spaces and training surrogates around expensive evaluations.
caveat: Requires model interfaces, configuration and domain-specific validation; probabilistic output is only as reliable as its assumptions.

name: SALib
summary: Python implementations of global sensitivity-analysis methods such as Sobol and Morris. Useful for ranking uncertain CFD inputs after sampling and evaluating a separate solver or surrogate model.
caveat: Generates designs and analyzes outputs; the user supplies solver runs and checks estimator convergence.

name: UQpy
summary: General Python toolbox for modelling uncertainty in physical and mathematical systems. Useful for uncertainty propagation and surrogate-based analyses around CFD models when sampling and probabilistic workflows need programmable control.
caveat: A general UQ library rather than a CFD package; connect and validate the simulation model separately.

name: DAFoam
summary: Adds discrete-adjoint capabilities to OpenFOAM-based multiphysics analysis with a Python interface for optimization. Supports aerodynamic, thermal and coupled design studies with many design variables.
caveat: Requires compatible OpenFOAM and optimization dependencies; convergence of the primal and adjoint problems matters for usable design gradients. Use the documented solver and dependency versions; verify adjoint gradients for the chosen objective and case.

name: DuMux
summary: Models porous-medium flow, transport and deformation with finite-volume and control-volume finite-element methods. Includes coupled multidomain formulations for applications that cross free-flow and porous regions.
caveat: The GitHub repository is an official mirror; primary development and issue tracking are hosted by the Stuttgart GitLab project.

name: IBAMR
summary: Combines immersed-boundary methods with Cartesian adaptive mesh refinement and distributed-memory parallelism. Useful for deformable structures interacting with fluids while retaining separate Eulerian and Lagrangian descriptions.
caveat: Requires a substantial numerical-library stack; discretization and coupling choices must match the stiffness, resolution and boundary conditions of the problem.

name: MRST
summary: Provides a MATLAB toolbox for flow, transport and mechanics in porous media. Includes modular reservoir and carbon-storage workflows that support numerical experimentation and model development.
caveat: Upstream recommends packaged releases for most users; compatibility with GNU Octave varies by module and should not be assumed.

name: oomph-lib
summary: Offers an object-oriented finite-element library with extensive multiphysics demonstration problems. Useful for building fluid-mechanics and fluid-structure models when researchers need control of the governing formulation.
caveat: A programmable numerical library rather than a turnkey engineering interface; model formulation and solver choices remain the user's responsibility.

name: OpenPNM
summary: Represents porous materials as pore networks and solves transport across them. Useful when investigating effective flow and transport properties without directly resolving every pore-scale fluid volume.
caveat: Network representations simplify pore geometry and physics; they are not interchangeable with fully resolved pore-scale Navier-Stokes simulations.

name: OPM Flow
summary: Implements reservoir flow simulation with automatic differentiation and established reservoir input formats. Useful for multiphase subsurface studies that need well models and reservoir-scale fluid transport.
caveat: Reservoir models operate under subsurface-flow assumptions and should not be substituted directly for free-fluid CFD.

name: preCICE
summary: Connects existing simulation programs through partitioned coupling, interface data exchange and mapping. Provides a common route to fluid-structure interaction, conjugate heat transfer and other coupled workflows.
caveat: A coupling library, not a CFD solver. Stable coupling still depends on compatible adapters, interface conditions and convergence settings.

name: solids4foam
summary: Extends the OpenFOAM ecosystem with solid-mechanics and fluid-solid interaction models. Provides tutorials for comparing partitioned coupling approaches and examining deformation-driven changes to a flow domain.
caveat: Compatibility is OpenFOAM-version dependent; verify the supported fork and version rather than mixing tutorial generations.

name: svMultiPhysics
summary: Provides coupled finite-element models for fluids, solids, diffusion and electrophysiology in cardiovascular research. Supports investigations where blood flow and deforming biological tissue must be modeled together.
caveat: Formerly svFSIplus; research software does not itself establish clinical suitability. Patient-specific predictions require separate validation and appropriate expertise.

name: ADCIRC
summary: Models time-dependent free-surface circulation and transport on unstructured finite-element grids. Common application areas include storm surge, tides, wind-driven circulation and coastal flooding studies.
caveat: Requires suitable meshes, forcing and calibration for the site; official documentation is being consolidated across several maintained sources.

name: ANUGA
summary: Solves shallow-water equations for floods, tsunamis and storm surges using finite-volume methods. Provides Python workflows and examples for combining terrain, boundary conditions and inundation studies.
caveat: Depth-averaged shallow-water assumptions do not resolve detailed vertical flow structure; terrain and boundary-data quality strongly affect inundation results.

name: CM1
summary: Supports idealized atmospheric experiments with a nonhydrostatic numerical model. Useful for studying convection, clouds and organized storms while controlling the background state and experimental forcing.
caveat: Primarily an idealized research model; configuring a real-time operational forecast is a different task from running its standard experiments.

name: Delft3D
summary: Collects Delft3D structured and flexible-mesh simulation engines for hydrodynamics, waves, morphology and water quality. Useful for integrated coastal, estuarine, river and urban water studies.
caveat: The source engines and packaged graphical interfaces have different delivery arrangements; component licensing and build requirements should be checked individually.

name: ERF
summary: Builds atmospheric-flow modeling on AMReX with adaptive meshes and a documented theory and examples. Relevant to energy-related atmospheric research and simulations requiring local resolution refinement.
caveat: Check the supported atmospheric models and boundary treatments for the intended application; the solver remains an evolving research code.

name: FUNWAVE-TVD
summary: Models dispersive nearshore waves with a Boussinesq-type formulation and shock-capturing treatment. Useful for wave transformation, coastal wave generation and studying processes beyond nondispersive shallow-water models.
caveat: Upstream labels the default branch beta and directs users to released versions. Confirm licensing and the release appropriate to your study.

name: GeoClaw
summary: Extends Clawpack for geophysical waves and flows, including tsunami propagation and inundation. Uses adaptive refinement to concentrate resolution where evolving waves and coastal interactions require it.
caveat: Depth-averaged flow assumptions and topographic resolution constrain the phenomena represented; assess the model for the intended hazard application.

name: Kynema-SGF (formerly AMR-Wind)
summary: Uses an adaptive structured-grid incompressible formulation for atmospheric boundary layers and wind-farm wakes. Can serve as the background flow solver in coupled blade-resolved wind-energy simulations.
best_for: Wind-farm wakes and atmospheric boundary layers
caveat: Renamed from AMR-Wind in 2026; actuator models and blade-resolved overset configurations represent different levels of physical detail.

name: Kynema-UGF (formerly Nalu-Wind)
summary: Provides an unstructured incompressible flow solver used in the Kynema wind-energy ecosystem. Useful for geometry-resolved turbine and energy-system flow calculations alongside structured background simulations.
caveat: Renamed from Nalu-Wind in 2026; coupled overset studies require additional ecosystem components and matching configuration.

name: MITgcm
summary: Models ocean and atmospheric circulation with a configurable numerical core and extensive verification examples. Useful across geophysical scales, including nonhydrostatic ocean processes and large-scale circulation.
best_for: Ocean circulation and geophysical fluid dynamics
caveat: Configuration, forcing and parameterizations determine the applicable scale; reproducing an experiment requires more than selecting a solver executable.

name: MOM6
summary: Solves ocean primitive equations with flexible vertical coordinates and options for coupled Earth-system configurations. Useful for ocean circulation studies and research into ocean-model numerics and parameterizations.
caveat: Designed for ocean primitive-equation modeling rather than general free-surface engineering CFD; regional setups need appropriate forcing and boundary data.

name: MPAS-Model
summary: Provides a shared unstructured-mesh framework with atmosphere, ocean and other geophysical model cores. Useful for multiscale circulation studies where mesh design and regional refinement matter.
caveat: Individual cores have separate build instructions, capabilities and data requirements; the shared repository is not a single universal model.

name: Proteus
summary: Separates continuum physical models from numerical methods in a Python-led toolkit. Includes multiphase Navier-Stokes, shallow-water and porous-flow formulations relevant to hydraulic and coastal research.
caveat: Broad method availability does not make every formulation suitable for every problem; external compiled dependencies are part of the installation.

name: SCHISM
summary: Uses unstructured grids for three-dimensional baroclinic circulation across connected river, estuary, shelf and ocean scales. Useful when one study spans several interacting hydrodynamic environments.
caveat: Choose supported modules and document forcing and vertical-grid assumptions; development-branch flags can change between model versions.

name: Thetis
summary: Builds coastal and estuarine flow models on Firedrake finite elements. Includes shallow-water, tracer, wetting-and-drying and adjoint capabilities for studying circulation and inverse problems.
caveat: Development versions may require matching Firedrake development branches; shallow-water assumptions must fit the intended physical scales.

name: WRF
summary: Provides the Weather Research and Forecasting modeling system for atmospheric research and numerical weather prediction. Useful when CFD studies need meteorological context or mesoscale flow conditions.
caveat: Meteorological predictions depend on initialization, forcing and physical parameterizations; WRF is not a replacement for geometry-resolved local engineering CFD.

name: ADflow
summary: Compressible Euler, laminar Navier-Stokes and RANS solver on structured multiblock and overset meshes, with a discrete adjoint and derivative-verification facilities for aerodynamic design optimization.
caveat: Targets structured and overset design workflows; a mesh generator and the surrounding MDO dependencies may be required for complete optimization studies.

name: code_saturne
summary: EDF's general-purpose CFD system for industrial flow and transport studies, providing finite-volume numerics, turbulence and heat-transfer models, parallel execution, and associated case setup tooling.
caveat: The project describes this GitHub repository as its public mirror; follow official release and contribution instructions rather than treating every branch as a release.

name: COOLFluiD
summary: Object-oriented high-performance platform for computational fluid dynamics, plasma and multiphysics simulations, exposing a modular research environment for developing and combining numerical methods and physical models.
caveat: Check the relevant plugin documentation and licensing details; this is a developer-oriented platform with a substantial build configuration.

name: Elmer FEM
summary: Multiphysics finite-element package combining fluid mechanics, heat transfer and other field solvers, with mesh and graphical tools plus parallel infrastructure for coupled scientific simulations.
caveat: Select the solver module, discretization and coupling strategy explicitly; breadth of available physics does not imply every coupling is turnkey.

name: FiPy
summary: Python finite-volume PDE framework from NIST for assembling coupled convection, diffusion, transient and source terms, particularly useful for transport, phase-field and materials-model prototyping and research.
caveat: A PDE-building framework rather than a complete industrial Navier-Stokes workflow; users must formulate and verify their coupled equations.

name: Fluidity
summary: Unstructured finite-element and control-volume CFD code with anisotropic mesh adaptivity, parallel execution and Python interfaces, used for multiphase, geophysical and general fluid-dynamics simulations.
caveat: The dependency and platform setup is substantial; use installation instructions matching the chosen branch and environment.

name: Kratos Multiphysics
summary: Modular C++ multiphysics framework with Python interfaces and dedicated fluid-dynamics, fluid-structure interaction and particle applications, supporting coupled engineering workflows and parallel simulation development.
caveat: Capabilities belong to specific applications; the core framework alone is not a configured CFD solver.

name: Lethe
summary: Finite-element CFD and discrete-element project using deal.II, with high-order continuous Galerkin formulations, adaptive meshes and coupled fluid-particle solvers for single-phase and multiphase engineering research.
caveat: Requires a compatible deal.II dependency stack; choose the relevant solver and reproduce its documented benchmark before extending a model.

name: MOOSE Navier-Stokes
summary: Navier-Stokes module within the MOOSE multiphysics framework, offering finite-element and finite-volume formulations for pressure-based, compressible and porous-flow applications with shared nonlinear-solver infrastructure and coupling mechanisms.
caveat: Read the module's solver-capability matrix: turbulence, two-phase and compressibility support varies between formulations and is actively evolving.

name: OpenFOAM Foundation
summary: Finite-volume CFD platform with an extensive solver, physical-model and meshing ecosystem, covering incompressible and compressible flows, turbulence, heat transfer, reacting systems and multiphase problems.
caveat: Foundation development branch; use a release for a fixed baseline. OpenCFD's separately maintained OpenFOAM distribution has a different upstream and release scheme.

name: SU2
summary: Multiphysics analysis and design suite centered on CFD and aerodynamic optimization, combining flow solvers, adjoint methods and Python-driven workflows for PDE-constrained engineering design studies.
caveat: Check the configuration and physical-model support for the specific SU2 release; example coverage does not establish accuracy for a new design.

name: CadQuery
summary: Python-based parametric CAD scripting built on Open CASCADE. Parameterized channels, nozzles and mechanical components can be generated consistently for geometry sweeps, automated studies and downstream mesh preparation.
caveat: Provides geometry construction rather than a CFD mesher or solver.

name: CGAL
summary: Computational geometry algorithms for triangulation, surface processing and mesh generation. Supplies robust geometric building blocks for custom CFD preprocessing tools rather than a single ready-made flow-analysis workflow.
caveat: License terms differ by CGAL package; check the specific component before integration.

name: FreeCAD
summary: Parametric solid modelling for engineering geometry, with editable design history and interoperable CAD workflows. Useful for preparing and revising fluid-domain boundaries before meshing rather than solving flow.
caveat: A CAD model is not automatically a watertight or appropriately resolved CFD domain.

name: IDWarp
summary: Deforms volume mesh nodes in response to surface perturbations using an inverse-distance approach. Useful for reusing a baseline CFD mesh during aerodynamic shape optimization and sensitivity calculations.
caveat: Large surface changes can still produce poor-quality or invalid cells; monitor mesh quality.

name: meshio
summary: Reads and writes many mesh formats through Python and a command-line interface. Helps move geometry, cells and associated fields between meshing tools, numerical solvers and visualization software.
caveat: Not every format preserves every field, boundary convention or high-order element representation.

name: Netgen
summary: Automatic tetrahedral mesh generation from constructive geometry, STL surfaces and CAD geometry. Python scripting, refinement and optimization make it useful for reproducible finite-element flow preprocessing.
caveat: Mesh topology, boundary tagging and wall-resolution requirements still need solver-specific checking.

name: pygalmesh
summary: Python interface to CGAL's mesh-generation capabilities, including primitive and implicit domains. Useful for constructing tetrahedral meshes from mathematical geometries and exporting them for numerical PDE experiments.
caveat: Sharp intersections and detailed meshing controls need care; this is not a CAD repair application.

name: pyGeo
summary: Geometry parameterization and geometric constraints for multidisciplinary optimization. Free-form deformation, CAD interfaces and design-variable handling connect aerodynamic shape changes to repeatable CFD and coupled engineering studies.
caveat: Individual CAD interfaces introduce their own installation and licensing requirements.

name: pygmsh
summary: Python geometry helpers around Gmsh reduce repetitive low-level entity bookkeeping. Useful for creating parameterized two- and three-dimensional domains and exporting meshes into automated numerical experiments.
caveat: Requires Gmsh; native Gmsh features and version compatibility should be checked for advanced workflows.

name: pyHyp
summary: Extrudes structured surface meshes into volume meshes using hyperbolic marching. Designed for the preprocessing stage of aerodynamic optimization workflows where body-fitted structured grids and controlled extrusion are useful.
caveat: Needs a suitable structured surface mesh; it is not an arbitrary-geometry unstructured mesher.

name: SALOME SMESH
summary: SALOME's mesh module creates, edits, imports and exports computational meshes, with grouping, quality controls and geometry integration. Supports preprocessing pipelines needing interactive inspection alongside structured automation.
best_for: Interactive mesh preparation and quality checks
caveat: Building the module requires additional SALOME components; the repository is not a standalone application installer.

name: trimesh
summary: Python tools for loading, inspecting and manipulating triangular surfaces. Helpful for checking imported STL geometry, connectivity and surface properties before committing to expensive volume meshing or flow calculations.
caveat: Surface processing does not establish CAD fidelity or the adequacy of a CFD boundary-layer mesh.

name: ExaDG
summary: Matrix-free high-order discontinuous Galerkin project whose core incompressible Navier-Stokes solver targets LES and DNS, with additional flow-transport, moving-mesh, fluid-structure and compressible-flow capabilities for research applications.
caveat: Best aligned with quadrilateral/hexahedral high-order discretizations; installation requires a compatible finite-element and linear-algebra dependency stack.

name: FLEXI
summary: Discontinuous Galerkin spectral-element framework for hyperbolic-parabolic conservation laws, emphasizing compressible CFD on unstructured hexahedral meshes with parallel execution and a supporting preprocessing and postprocessing suite.
caveat: Uses a specific high-order mesh and preprocessing workflow; check the required HOPR and HDF5 versions for the chosen release.

name: HORSES3D
summary: Fortran DG spectral-element multiphysics solver for compressible and incompressible flows, with polynomial adaptivity, turbulence closures and diffuse-interface multiphase formulations on curvilinear hexahedral meshes using hybrid CPU parallelism.
caveat: The CPU repository and separate GPU project have different supported paths; verify that a desired feature is available in the selected implementation.

name: MIRGE-Com
summary: Python-driven discontinuous Galerkin simulation application for compressible viscous and inviscid reactive mixtures, using unstructured meshes and accelerator-oriented infrastructure for exascale-enabled scramjet and fluid-flow research.
best_for: Research on reacting compressible DG solvers
caveat: Research application with a specialized array, mesh and code-generation stack; inspect supported chemistry and transport assumptions before selecting it for a study.

name: Nek5000
summary: Spectral-element solver for incompressible and low-Mach flows, scalar transport and conjugate heat transfer, using high-order tensor-product elements and parallel algorithms suited to turbulence research.
best_for: High-order incompressible DNS and heat transfer
caveat: Classic CPU-oriented Nek implementation; mesh and polynomial resolution must be selected for the intended flow and turbulence regime.

name: nekRS
summary: High-order spectral-element CFD solver for incompressible and low-Mach flow, with OCCA-based CPU and GPU backends, scalar transport, turbulence models and conjugate heat-transfer capabilities on HPC systems.
caveat: Follow the release notes and backend requirements; the project distinguishes stable master from preview development and does not support every desktop platform.

name: PyFR
summary: Flux-reconstruction CFD platform for high-order scale-resolving flow simulations on unstructured mixed-element meshes, with code-generated computational kernels and multiple CPU and GPU execution backends for heterogeneous systems.
caveat: Backend, mesh-element and equation-system support depend on the selected release; compare cost at equivalent accuracy rather than polynomial order alone.

name: Trixi.jl
summary: Julia framework for high-order conservation-law simulations, combining discontinuous Galerkin and related methods, adaptive tree-based meshes and an extensible equation interface for compressible-flow and numerical-method research.
caveat: Check equation, mesh and backend compatibility in the documentation; Julia's first-run compilation cost should be separated from steady-state timings.

name: UCNS3D
summary: Unstructured compressible-flow solver offering high-order finite-volume reconstruction and discontinuous Galerkin methods, mixed-element meshes, turbulence models and MPI/OpenMP execution for aerodynamic and multicomponent-flow research in two or three dimensions.
best_for: High-order compressible CFD on mixed meshes
caveat: Build bounds can be case-specific, and accelerator offload covers selected paths rather than every solver mode; follow the current build instructions.

name: DualSPHysics
summary: Smoothed-particle hydrodynamics solver using C++, CUDA and OpenMP, with engineering workflows focused on free surfaces, wave interactions and large-deformation fluid motion around moving bodies and structures.
caveat: The complete user distribution includes associated tools beyond the source repository; particle resolution, artificial compressibility and boundary treatment require case-specific assessment. Particle resolution, boundary treatment and weak-compressibility settings influence results; GPU builds require a supported CUDA toolchain.

name: FluidX3D
summary: OpenCL lattice-Boltzmann flow simulator with CPU and GPU execution, integrated visualization, free-surface and thermal extensions, and tools for importing triangulated geometry into a Cartesian lattice for interactive studies.
caveat: Source-available with a non-commercial restriction, explicitly not OSI open source. Check its current license before use; the documented solver has no checkpoint/restart support.

name: GPUSPH
summary: CUDA implementation of weakly compressible smoothed-particle hydrodynamics, providing GPU-oriented infrastructure for free-surface flow simulations and research involving moving boundaries and fluid interactions with engineering geometries.
caveat: CUDA hardware and a compatible compiler stack are required; establish the chosen formulation's resolution and compressibility error for the case.

name: HemoCell
summary: Cell-resolved suspension framework coupling Palabos lattice-Boltzmann fluid dynamics to deformable Lagrangian cell membranes through immersed boundaries, with dedicated models and parallel data management for blood-flow research.
caveat: A specialized cellular-flow model, not a clinical prediction tool; inspect cell mechanics, material parameters and case-specific validation requirements.

name: Lettuce
summary: PyTorch-based lattice-Boltzmann framework for two- and three-dimensional fluid simulations, enabling Python prototyping, GPU execution and experiments connecting kinetic flow solvers with neural networks and automatic differentiation.
caveat: Check current PyTorch/CUDA compatibility and whether custom kernels support the intended differentiable workflow; default installation targets specific CUDA versions.

name: NATriuM
summary: High-order off-lattice Boltzmann research solver based on deal.II, supporting unstructured two- and three-dimensional grids through discontinuous-Galerkin or semi-Lagrangian streaming for weakly and fully compressible viscous flows.
caveat: Authors explicitly warn that the code is early-stage and they are unlikely to answer questions; treat it as a research reference with limited support.

name: PySPH
summary: Python framework for defining particle equations and integrators, generating compiled Cython or OpenCL kernels, and running several SPH formulations with optional shared-memory and distributed parallelism for research simulations.
caveat: Different bundled SPH formulations make different assumptions; compare conservation, convergence and boundary behavior for the scheme actually used. A method-development framework: selecting an available formulation does not establish suitability for a particular engineering problem.

name: Sailfish
summary: GPU lattice-Boltzmann simulation package with a Python-driven setup and CUDA or OpenCL execution, providing examples for exploring kinetic flow models and generated computational kernels on supported accelerators.
caveat: Legacy dependency and GPU-toolchain assumptions need checking before adoption; its historical examples should not be assumed compatible with a current Python environment.

name: SPHinXsys
summary: C++ multiphysics library built around smoothed-particle hydrodynamics, providing unified discretizations and strongly coupled fluid, solid and multibody models together with examples and a Python interface for engineering studies.
caveat: Select the specific formulation and tested example family; a common particle framework does not eliminate resolution or coupling-error studies. Research and engineering library with model-specific assumptions; choose examples matching the intended constitutive laws and flow regime.

name: DAPPER
summary: Experimental data-assimilation framework with ensemble and variational methods, diagnostics and model examples. Useful for learning state estimation and testing assimilation ideas on geophysical-fluid prototypes before solver-specific integration.
caveat: Designed for teaching and fundamental experiments; coupling production CFD requires additional implementation.

name: DeepXDE
summary: Scientific machine-learning library supporting physics-informed networks and neural operators. Includes differential-equation workflows useful for fluid inverse problems, parameter estimation and exploratory surrogate studies with explicit boundary and initial conditions.
caveat: PINN training convergence is problem dependent; verify predictions against trusted numerical or experimental references.

name: EZyRB
summary: Data-driven reduced-basis modelling from parameterized numerical snapshots. Useful for constructing nonintrusive CFD surrogates when full-order results are available but modifying the original governing-equation implementation is impractical.
caveat: Prediction quality depends on snapshot coverage; extrapolation beyond the training parameter range needs testing.

name: ITHACA-FV
summary: OpenFOAM-based reduced-order-modelling framework with methods for developing compact finite-volume models. Useful for experimenting with projection, parameterized flow snapshots and reduced solvers close to existing OpenFOAM workflows.
caveat: Check the supported OpenFOAM release and rebuild dependencies for the selected branch.

name: NeuralOperator
summary: Official neural-operator library containing Fourier Neural Operators and related architectures. Useful for learning mappings between PDE inputs and solution fields, including fluid and transport surrogate research.
caveat: Resolution transfer does not guarantee accuracy under new geometries, regimes or boundary conditions.

name: NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo
summary: PyTorch-based physics machine-learning framework with reusable models and training recipes. Aerodynamics examples make it relevant to surface and volume surrogates, scalable training and engineering field prediction.
caveat: GPU requirements, model prerequisites and separate dataset terms vary across examples.

name: PDEArena
summary: Training and evaluation framework for neural PDE modelling, with architecture collections and fluid datasets. Useful for controlled comparisons of learned Navier–Stokes and shallow-water evolution models across spatial and temporal scales.
caveat: Research benchmarks and trained models do not establish performance on industrial geometries or operating regimes.

name: PhiFlow
summary: Differentiable simulation toolkit integrated with NumPy and machine-learning frameworks. Provides fluid examples and automatic differentiation pathways useful for inverse problems, learned corrections and optimization through simulations.
caveat: Choose the numerical model and discretization for the intended physics; differentiability alone does not establish fidelity.

name: PyDMD
summary: Dynamic mode decomposition tools for extracting coherent spatial and temporal structures from snapshot data. Useful for analyzing CFD transients, building data-driven reduced models and comparing modal representations.
caveat: Mode estimates depend on sampling, noise and preprocessing; the fitted dynamics need independent validation.

name: pyMOR
summary: Model-order-reduction library using abstract interfaces to connect numerical algorithms and PDE backends. Supports reduced bases, POD and system-theoretic approaches for constructing compact parameterized flow or transport models.
caveat: Connecting a new CFD solver requires compatible operators, data access and suitable reduction assumptions.

name: PySINDy
summary: Sparse system-identification tools for discovering compact dynamical models from data. Useful for fluid reduced coordinates and PDE-discovery experiments where interpretable model structure is preferable to a black-box surrogate.
caveat: Derivative estimation, noise and candidate-library choices strongly affect discovered equations.

name: Transolver
summary: Research implementation of transformer-based PDE modelling on general geometries. Includes airfoil and car-flow design experiments, making it useful for studying geometry-aware surrogates alongside established neural-operator baselines.
caveat: Published benchmark claims belong to the original study; reproduce the selected task before relying on generalization.

name: CFDEM coupling PUBLIC
summary: Couples OpenFOAM flow calculations with discrete particle dynamics through selectable force and data-exchange models. Useful for studying fluidized beds, particulate transport and fluid-particle interaction workflows.
caveat: Public and commercial product capabilities differ. Verify the documented OpenFOAM and particle-solver versions before installation.

name: JAX-Fluids
summary: Implements differentiable compressible flow simulation with high-order reconstruction, level-set and diffuse-interface two-phase methods. Enables research connecting numerical fluid dynamics, automatic differentiation and accelerator-based computation.
caveat: Differentiating a discrete solver does not automatically yield reliable gradients through shocks or interface events; examine discretization and sensitivity assumptions.

name: Mantaflow
summary: Combines a fluid-simulation core with Python scene definitions and an extensible plugin system. Supports liquid, smoke and learning experiments aimed at graphics-oriented fluid algorithm research.
caveat: Designed primarily for computer-graphics research; attractive visual output alone does not establish engineering accuracy.

name: MFC
summary: Solves compressible multiphase flows with interface models, bubble dynamics, phase-change options and particle tracking. Useful for investigating shock-interface interaction and other strongly compressible multiphase phenomena.
caveat: Different mixture, interface and bubble models make different assumptions; select the model appropriate to the physical scale and regime.

name: SPlisHSPlasH
summary: Implements several incompressible SPH pressure solvers alongside viscosity, surface tension and rigid or deformable body coupling. Particularly useful for comparing particle-fluid simulation methods and visual experiments.
best_for: SPH incompressibility and coupled particle scenes
caveat: Originates in physically based graphics research; engineering use needs independent dimensional, resolution and validation checks.

name: ABLATE
summary: Develops reacting-flow capabilities around turbulent mixing, fuel entrainment and ablative boundary layers. Offers a research entry point for studying combustion environments associated with hybrid rocket motors.
caveat: Research-oriented software; use documented examples and confirm the available physical models before planning a new application.

name: Cantera
summary: Provides thermochemistry, transport properties, reaction mechanisms, reactor networks and one-dimensional flames. A practical foundation for checking chemistry assumptions before embedding them in a reacting-flow solver.
caveat: Not a general three-dimensional CFD solver; mechanism suitability must be assessed for the intended conditions.

name: Fire Dynamics Simulator
summary: Models low-speed fire-driven flows with large-eddy simulation, emphasizing smoke and heat transport. Its documentation includes separate verification and validation material for assessing intended fire-engineering applications.
caveat: A low-speed fire model rather than a general shock or detonation solver. Safety-critical conclusions require qualified interpretation and appropriate validation.

name: PeleC
summary: Solves compressible reacting flows using block-structured adaptive meshes and embedded boundaries. Connects detailed chemistry to flow calculations where acoustic waves and compressibility are physically important.
caveat: Requires the AMReX, PelePhysics and SUNDIALS stack; mesh, chemistry and temporal resolution need problem-specific assessment.

name: PeleLMeX
summary: Combines a low-Mach reacting-flow formulation with adaptive refinement and embedded boundaries. Targets flame-turbulence research while avoiding the acoustic time-scale restriction of a fully compressible formulation.
caveat: The low-Mach formulation is unsuitable when shocks or strong acoustic coupling govern the physics. Use the documented model assumptions.

name: PelePhysics
summary: Supplies thermodynamics, transport, chemistry generation and additional spray, soot and radiation modules shared by Pele solvers. Useful when researching combustion models rather than duplicating property implementations.
caveat: A supporting physics library rather than a complete standalone CFD application; module support differs between Pele solvers.

name: pyJac
summary: Generates analytical Jacobian source code for chemical reaction mechanisms. Helps researchers examine the expensive derivative calculations that arise inside stiff chemical-kinetics integrators and reacting-flow applications.
caveat: An older research tool with version-sensitive dependencies; generated code and mechanism support should be checked in the target environment.

name: pyMARS
summary: Reduces detailed chemical mechanisms using graph-based methods and sensitivity analysis. Useful for preparing smaller chemistry models when detailed mechanisms make reacting-flow or reactor studies too expensive.
caveat: Reduction accuracy depends on the selected targets and training conditions; validate the reduced mechanism over the intended operating envelope.

name: Reaction Mechanism Generator
summary: Constructs chemical kinetic mechanisms using reaction families and thermochemical data. Supports upstream chemistry development for combustion studies before mechanism reduction, reactor assessment or coupling to CFD.
caveat: Generated mechanisms are hypotheses requiring assessment against suitable data; this is not a spatial CFD solver.

name: Spitfire
summary: Builds tabulated chemistry models and integrates chemistry or reaction-diffusion systems. Particularly relevant to nonpremixed flamelet libraries used to reduce the cost of larger fire simulations.
caveat: Tables remain specific to their generating assumptions, mechanism and parameter range; extrapolation requires separate assessment.

name: TChem
summary: Provides chemical source terms, thermodynamic properties, Jacobians and canonical reactor formulations for complex kinetic mechanisms. Useful for integrating and studying the stiff chemistry component of reacting simulations.
best_for: Chemical kinetics kernels and reactor models
caveat: Distinguish this kinetics toolkit from the separate TChem-atm atmospheric-chemistry project; it does not supply a complete spatial flow solver.

name: AFiD
summary: Parallel finite-difference flow solver for Rayleigh-Benard convection and Taylor-Couette turbulence, built around distributed decompositions and FFT-based algorithms for large canonical direct numerical simulations on HPC systems.
caveat: Specialized canonical-flow geometry and boundary conditions; check variant-specific documentation and dependencies rather than treating it as a general geometry solver.

name: CaNS
summary: Parallel incompressible Navier-Stokes solver designed for canonical-flow DNS, using a structured finite-difference discretization and efficient pressure solution with CPU and GPU-oriented implementations for turbulence research at scale.
caveat: Targets canonical structured domains; check grid, boundary-condition and accelerator constraints instead of assuming arbitrary industrial geometry support.

name: Dedalus
summary: Spectral PDE framework with symbolic equation specification and parallel execution, supporting fluid-dynamics research across Cartesian and curved domains rather than restricting users to one fixed equation set.
caveat: Users formulate equations, gauge conditions and boundary constraints; this flexibility is not a substitute for checking mathematical well-posedness and numerical convergence.

name: FluidSim
summary: Python framework for reproducible fluid-dynamics simulations with extensible solvers, MPI-enabled pseudospectral methods, and integrated output and analysis workflows for turbulence and geophysical-flow research across multiple model equations.
caveat: Official publish-only GitHub mirror; canonical development and contributions are on the project's Heptapod Mercurial repository.

name: IAMR
summary: Parallel adaptive-mesh code for variable-density incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, providing an AMReX-based route to locally refined flow simulations and exploration of block-structured algorithms for research applications.
caveat: Variable-density incompressibility is a modeling assumption, not a fully compressible shock-capturing formulation; check the examples and required AMReX revision.

name: incflo
summary: AMReX-based incompressible Navier-Stokes application for flows in complex geometries, combining block-structured adaptive-grid infrastructure with embedded boundaries and shared hydrodynamic utilities for parallel CPU and GPU research.
caveat: Requires compatible AMReX and AMReX-Hydro versions; follow project instructions for supported solvers and boundary conditions rather than assuming general model coverage.

name: Oceananigans.jl
summary: Julia software for incompressible geophysical fluid dynamics on CPU and GPU hardware, supporting Cartesian and spherical-shell domains, turbulence studies and ocean-oriented models with programmable simulation workflows.
caveat: Ocean-oriented incompressible and hydrostatic/nonhydrostatic modeling assumptions differ from general compressible industrial CFD; choose the documented model appropriate to the scales. Its documented ocean and Boussinesq formulations do not cover arbitrary compressible engineering flows.

name: OpenSBLI
summary: Python code-generation framework translating symbolic compressible-flow equations into parallel high-order finite-difference solvers, with structured curvilinear multiblock meshes and WENO or TENO shock-capturing options for heterogeneous computing architectures.
caveat: Generated solvers depend on a compatible parallel runtime and compiler stack; changing symbolic equations still requires numerical verification.

name: Pencil Code
summary: Modular high-order finite-difference code for compressible hydrodynamics with magnetic fields and particles, offering MPI-parallel infrastructure and many sample configurations for turbulence and astrophysical-fluid research on distributed systems.
caveat: The project documents its own source-management and contribution workflow; numerical diffusion and shock treatment must be selected for the intended regime.

name: spectralDNS
summary: Python collection of parallel spectral Navier-Stokes and related solvers, providing an inspectable environment for direct numerical simulation and experiments with spectral discretization and time-integration methods.
caveat: Research-oriented solver collection; verify the maintained solver path and current shenfun/MPI dependency compatibility for the intended example.

name: WaterLily.jl
summary: Julia solver for unsteady incompressible viscous flow around dynamic immersed bodies, using Cartesian grids, geometric multigrid pressure solves and backend-agnostic CPU or GPU execution in two or three dimensions.
caveat: An immersed Cartesian-grid method rather than a body-fitted mesh solver; quantify boundary and grid-resolution effects for the target geometry.

name: Xcompact3d / Incompact3d
summary: High-order compact finite-difference framework for turbulent-flow DNS and LES, combining Cartesian-grid efficiency, distributed-memory parallelism and immersed-boundary treatments for research on incompressible flows and complex geometries.
caveat: The named repository is the CPU solver; inspect the separate accelerator developments rather than assuming identical GPU capabilities.

name: CFD Python
summary: A notebook sequence teaching CFD through incremental PDE implementations, culminating in Navier–Stokes exercises. Useful for understanding discretization, numerical diffusion and convergence before adopting larger solver frameworks.
caveat: Educational discretizations and small examples are not production CFD solvers.

name: CFDBench
summary: Fluid-dynamics surrogate benchmark with cavity, tube, dam and cylinder cases across boundary conditions, geometries and physical properties. Includes datasets and baseline implementations for studying inference-time generalization.
caveat: Original data generation uses commercial ICEM/Fluent; using released data has separate download and storage requirements.

name: FEniCSx Tutorial
summary: Executable finite-element tutorial covering DOLFINx fundamentals and Navier–Stokes examples. Useful for deriving weak forms, applying boundary conditions and exploring transparent flow implementations with associated explanations and parallel execution.
caveat: Follow the tutorial's supported DOLFINx version; examples are not a universal production flow solver.

name: Giverny / JHTDB access
summary: Python and MATLAB access tools for querying the Johns Hopkins Turbulence Database. Enables sampled DNS fields and cutouts for turbulence analysis, numerical comparisons and data-driven research without downloading entire simulations.
caveat: Access tokens, query-size limits and available variables depend on the service and chosen dataset.

name: MASA
summary: Library of manufactured analytical solutions and source terms for PDE software verification. Includes Euler, Navier–Stokes and turbulence-model formulations useful for checking implementation errors and observed convergence orders.
caveat: Manufactured solutions verify equation implementation; they do not validate physical modelling against experiments.

name: NekExamples
summary: Official Nek5000 examples with case descriptions and required simulation files. Includes canonical and turbulent-flow setups useful for learning spectral-element workflows, inspecting boundary conditions and checking an installation.
caveat: Examples require Nek5000 and case-specific preparation; confirm mesh resolution and expected reference quantities.

name: PDEBench
summary: Scientific machine-learning benchmark combining PDE datasets, data-generation code and baseline models. Fluid cases and varied initial, boundary and physical parameters support repeatable comparisons of learned flow prediction methods.
caveat: Datasets are hosted separately and can be large; check documented environment and data-path requirements.

name: preCICE Tutorials
summary: Worked coupled-simulation cases using preCICE with real solvers, including fluid–structure and thermal applications. Useful for understanding participant configuration, adapter interfaces and reproducible multiphysics setup rather than isolated equations.
caveat: Most tutorials need multiple solver installations and adapters with compatible versions.

name: Riemann Problems and Jupyter Solutions
summary: Interactive notebook book covering Riemann problems for hyperbolic equations, including acoustics, shallow water and Euler flow. Useful for understanding wave structure and comparing exact or approximate flux solvers.
caveat: Text and executable code have separate license files; consult both when reusing material.

name: Riemann-Solvers
summary: Compact implementations accompanying classical Riemann-solver methods for advection, Burgers and Euler equations. Useful for comparing schemes and developing intuition about shocks, rarefactions and numerical fluxes.
caveat: No repository-level license was apparent in the inspected listing; inspect permissions before copying code.

name: SU2 TestCases
summary: Official collection of SU2 test inputs spanning flow, adjoints, conjugate heat transfer and other capabilities. Useful for reproducing regression cases and finding solver-specific examples matched to SU2 development.
caveat: Match the case branch or revision to the SU2 solver version; a regression pass is not physical validation.

name: ADIOS2
summary: Scalable scientific input/output framework transporting self-describing variables through files, networks and memory. Useful for large CFD output pipelines, streaming analysis and reducing coupling between simulation and data consumers.
caveat: Requires integration into the application or an existing compatible I/O path.

name: CGNS
summary: Defines and implements a standard for storing CFD meshes, flow solutions and related metadata. Useful when interoperability and consistent exchange between preprocessing, simulation and postprocessing tools matter.
caveat: A data model and library, not a solver; interoperable use still depends on supported CGNS conventions.

name: netCDF4-Python
summary: Python and NumPy interface to the netCDF library. Useful for reading, writing and inspecting array-based simulation datasets, especially geophysical and atmospheric fluid workflows using netCDF conventions.
caveat: Respect netCDF thread-safety limitations and preserve units, coordinates and metadata conventions.

name: ParaView
summary: Scientific visualization application built on VTK, supporting large-data analysis and programmable pipelines. Widely useful for CFD field inspection, slices, streamlines, time histories and reproducible postprocessing workflows.
caveat: Official GitHub mirror; upstream development and issue reporting take place on Kitware GitLab.

name: PyVista
summary: NumPy-friendly Python interface to VTK datasets, filters and plotting. Supports scripted extraction, slicing and interactive display of CFD meshes and fields in notebooks, applications or automated reporting.
caveat: Headless rendering and remote notebook use may require additional graphics configuration.

name: trame
summary: Python framework for interactive scientific web applications, integrating VTK and ParaView rendering. Useful for turning CFD analysis pipelines into browser-accessible viewers with local or remote visualization.
caveat: Application deployment, authentication and resource limits need separate design for public-facing services.

name: vedo
summary: Python scientific visualization built on VTK and NumPy, with mesh manipulation and analysis helpers. Useful for compact exploratory scripts, interactive inspection and presentation of surfaces or volumetric flow data.
caveat: Check supported readers and field association conventions against the output format of your solver.

name: VisIt
summary: Scientific visualization and analysis application for mesh-based simulation data. Useful for exploring large CFD datasets, applying derived quantities and building repeatable analysis routines across supported simulation formats.
caveat: Solver output must match a supported reader or be converted to an appropriate exchange format.

name: VTK
summary: Visualization and data-processing toolkit for building scientific applications. Provides meshes, filters, rendering and file readers that underpin custom CFD postprocessing tools and many established visualization applications.
caveat: A development toolkit rather than a complete end-user CFD application; GitHub is an official mirror.

name: yt
summary: Python analysis and visualization for volumetric simulation datasets, including adaptive meshes. Useful for derived fields, spatial selections, profiles and volume rendering in computational astrophysics and related fluid simulations.
caveat: Strongest fit is supported volumetric simulation formats; confirm a frontend exists for your solver.

name: AMReX
summary: Block-structured adaptive-mesh framework supplying parallel data structures, particles, embedded boundaries and CPU/GPU infrastructure for building CFD applications; it does not provide a single configured flow model.
caveat: Application developers must supply governing equations, discretizations and physical models. Match the framework revision and accelerator configuration to the consuming solver.

name: PETSc
summary: Parallel numerical toolkit providing sparse algebra, nonlinear solvers, time integration and distributed meshes for CFD implementations; application code still supplies the flow equations, discretization and boundary conditions.
caveat: Official GitHub mirror; primary development and issue tracking are on GitLab. Solver/preconditioner choices and nullspace handling must match the discretized problem.

name: hypre
summary: Parallel sparse-system library featuring algebraic and structured multigrid methods, useful for CFD pressure and diffusion solves; it supplies numerical components rather than a turnkey fluid simulation.
caveat: Select an interface and preconditioner appropriate to matrix structure and symmetry; GPU support varies by algorithm and build. Current licensing is Apache-2.0 OR MIT.

name: Ginkgo
summary: C++ sparse linear-algebra library targeting many-core CPUs and GPUs, useful inside CFD pressure or coupled-system solvers; users provide matrices and algorithms appropriate to their discretized equations.
caveat: A linear-algebra backend, not a CFD application. Benchmark complete solver convergence and data movement; accelerator support does not guarantee faster end-to-end simulation.

name: MFEM
summary: Modular parallel finite-element library with high-order spaces, adaptive meshes and operator infrastructure for developing CFD discretizations; examples and miniapps are building blocks rather than complete engineering workflows.
caveat: Users select stable spaces, weak forms, boundary conditions and solvers. Reproducing an example does not establish the suitability of a newly assembled flow formulation.

name: deal.II
summary: C++ adaptive finite-element library providing meshes, finite-element spaces, assembly and parallel algorithms for custom CFD programs, including documented flow examples rather than one universal ready-to-run solver.
caveat: A numerical development library; the application determines governing equations and stable discretization. Optional PETSc, Trilinos and p4est dependencies must be version-compatible.

name: DOLFINx / FEniCSx
summary: C++ and Python finite-element environment for expressing and assembling PDE problems, useful for programmable Navier-Stokes studies; users still formulate weak forms, constraints, boundary conditions and solver strategies.
caveat: DOLFINx is the FEniCSx computational component, not a standalone packaged CFD model. Follow documentation matching the installed release and compatible FEniCSx dependencies.

name: libCEED
summary: Library for factored finite-element operator evaluation across CPU and GPU backends, enabling matrix-free high-order CFD implementations; its algebraic interface integrates into applications rather than defining their complete physics.
caveat: Applications retain mesh, parallel decomposition and solver responsibilities. Backend behavior and deterministic capabilities vary; bundled fluid miniapps illustrate integration rather than certify arbitrary CFD models.

name: Kokkos Core
summary: C++ performance-portability programming library abstracting parallel execution and memory layouts, useful for implementing CFD kernels across CPU and GPU architectures; it supplies no governing equations or flow solver.
caveat: Performance portability still requires algorithm, layout and backend choices. Check compiler and device support for the chosen release; numerical correctness remains the application's responsibility.

name: SUNDIALS
summary: Time-integration and nonlinear-solver libraries for differential and algebraic systems, useful for stiff chemistry and semidiscrete CFD equations; applications supply spatial operators, physical models and appropriate solver interfaces.
caveat: Not a spatial CFD solver. Choose tolerances, Jacobians, vector backends and preconditioners for the actual stiffness and conservation requirements; keep package versions consistent.

name: p4est
summary: Parallel forest-of-octrees library managing adaptive mesh refinement, coarsening and partitioning, useful beneath scalable CFD discretizations; the consuming application supplies numerical fluxes, physical fields and time evolution.
caveat: Mesh infrastructure rather than a flow solver. Official guidance warns that auto-generated GitHub source archives lack required components; use maintained release tarballs or initialize dependencies correctly.
